purpose: Erythromycin is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections, including chest infections, throat infections, skin infections, and sexually transmitted infections like chlamydia. It can also be used in people who are allergic to penicillin as an alternative antibiotic. Sometimes it is used to help the stomach empty more quickly in people who have a condition called gastroparesis.
how_it_works: Erythromycin works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply. Without these proteins, the bacteria cannot survive and your immune system can clear the infection more easily. It does not kill bacteria directly but slows them down enough that your body can fight them off.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are stomach-related and include nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, and diarrhea. These tend to happen more often if you take it on an empty stomach. Some people may also notice a mild skin rash or headache.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have heart rhythm problems, liver disease, or are taking other medications, as erythromycin can interact with many common drugs and may affect your heart rhythm in rare cases. Avoid taking it with certain medications like statins, blood thinners, or other antibiotics without checking with your pharmacist first. If you develop severe diarrhea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or an irregular heartbeat, contact your doctor right away. Always finish the full course even if you feel better, to prevent antibiotic resistance.
typical_dosing: The typical adult dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken by mouth every 6 hours, or up to 4 times a day, depending on the type and severity of the infection. It is usually taken for 7 to 14 days. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach upset. Always follow the exact instructions your doctor or pharmacist gives you.
